analysis:
Reviewed the new GemmaCheck.swift (qualification/diagnostic CLI subcommand `gemma`, lines 1-500) and the TensorParallelCheck.swift dispatch change (adds `gemma` route before Options parsing, ~line 526). This is an offline developer/qualification tool in the TensorParallelCheck target, not the provider serving path (TB-002 coordinator WebSocket, TB-011 App Attest authorization, TB-012/013 add-on). I saw no coordinator/consumer-facing input, no network listener beyond the existing QwenTensorParallelGroup backends (ring/socket over 127.0.0.1, jaccl), and no change to provider keys, attestation, or authorization.

Observed controls: request file capped at 1 MiB (line 167); prompt digest verified; outputCount/chunkSize bounded 1..4096; deadline bounded 30..7200 s and armed via ProcessDeadline; report path must not already exist (line 143); synthesize requires an absolute new output path. Ranks agree on workload/config/arithmetic via digest exchange before loading (line 202). The sealed-bench path uses the existing BENCH codec with an unauthenticated ephemeral key exchange. The code and notes label it as cost measurement only and never a product trust, so there is no new trust claim. Reports name roles and chips only, with no host, address or path (line 51). `createFile` for the report uses default permissions (not 0o600); the contents are token IDs and logits for synthetic or qualification prompts, which is low sensitivity. Reports could carry model output logits for real prompts if the operator runs real data, but this is an operator-run local diagnostic. The socket backend binding to 127.0.0.1 is in the unseen QwenTensorParallelGroup. Prefix-repeat uses the in-process prompt-prefix tier. Whether it touches the encrypted SSD cache (T-041) is outside the supplied evidence; the tool describes it as the rank's memory tier.

Remaining unverified: the Gemma4TensorParallelModel, Gemma4TensorParallelLocalPair, and the QualificationComparator implementations are not in the supplied evidence, so their internals were not reviewed. No findings.
